name: message
title: Message
purpose: Present normalized user, assistant, and system message content with quiet role hierarchy, bounded rich content, event-level status, and optional identity, metadata, actions, and recovery without calling a model or platform service.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Semantic article bound to normalized runtime message state.

anatomy.name: avatar
anatomy.description: Optional decorative or product identity mark.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.description: Primary message content and rich renderer boundary.

anatomy.name: state
anatomy.description: Streaming, failure, interruption, and recovery region.

anatomy.name: actions
anatomy.description: Actions applying to the message content.

slots.description: Timestamp, model, source, or other secondary context.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Copy, feedback, retry, citation, or product actions.

slots.name: recovery
slots.description: Retry or alternate action for failed or interrupted output.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Partial content and restrained progress indication.

states.description: Retained partial content and explicit interruption status.

states.name: failed

states.name: long-content

themes.name: high-contrast
themes.description: Strengthened status, focus, and boundary distinction.

viewports.name: mobile
viewports.expectation: User width remains bounded and actions are touch-safe without page overflow.

viewports.name: tablet
viewports.expectation: Content and action alignment remain visually connected.

viewports.name: wide
viewports.expectation: Prose does not expand to an unreadable line length.

accessibility.semantics: Uses a semantic message article with normalized role context, bounded content, visible error text, keyboard-reachable actions, and one optional polite status announcement that does not include token-by-token deltas.
keyboard: Tab reaches each message action and recovery control in visual order.
Hover-disclosed actions also appear on focus-within and remain discoverable on touch layouts.
Custom content does not trap focus inside code, links, or embedded renderers.
focus: Message actions and recovery controls retain visible focus in every declared theme.
Streaming, completion, failure, and interruption do not move focus.
Removing transient status never removes the currently focused action.

motion.contract: Entry and streaming indicators use bounded transform or opacity; content deltas do not animate and reduced motion disables nonessential movement.

scenarios.name: long-content
